liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): The pre-verse jam, roughly minutes 3 to 12, develops rapidly into a chaotic yet tight funky groove; Jerry plays a pronounced tease of King Crimson's 'Fracture' around the 22-23 minute mark [16][17][20]
- **Row Jimmy** (1 review): Reviewer's highlight is Row Jimmy into Dew, with Jerry in control and the band following [24]
- **El Paso** (1 review): The El Paso serves as a perfect high-energy break in the middle of the Dark Star madness [19]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): By 1973 standards, the Eyes is somewhat unfocused and the Dew a little sloppy [16]

## The recordings

- **gd73-08-01.sbd.cotsman.12222.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 175 min; rated 4.37/5 by 46 [1]. Said about its sound: The Dark Star through Dew section was remastered by David Gans and sounds spectacular; the mix feels like sitting at Billy's drum kit; A couple of glitches early in the show clear up quickly, and the recording then sounds really good; The recording is mostly soundboard with enough audience mixed in to feel like being there, neither plastic nor distant [14][15][23][24]
- **gd1973-08-01.sbd.sirmick.patch-12222.92478.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 4.6/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Missing first notes of Goin' Down the Road were patched in from the audience source and the track pitch adjusted [2]
- **gd1973-08-01.aud.weiner.8724.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 171 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [10]. Said about its sound: Mic cable dropouts in Race Is On, Bird Song, Casey Jones and Around and Around were cross-faded [10]
- **gd1973-08-01.sbd.kaplan.11813.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 157 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [11]. Said about its sound: The soundboard is complete except for the opening set-one songs Promised Land, Sugaree, Race Is On and You Ain't Woman Enough [11]

## Around the show

- The show fell on Jerry's birthday, and the band seemed to feel it [15]
- Jerry played on his birthday in 1973 [24]
- The reviewer links this night's creative configuration to earlier days and points to Watkins Glen on 7-14-73 [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-08-01.sbd.cotsman.12222.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard with audience patches [1]. Also: Complete show compiled from the latest soundboard sources with audience patches, from S. Kaplan and N. Weiner seeds; seeded to etree by JCotsman [1]
- **gd1973-08-01.sbd.sirmick.patch-12222.92478.sbeok.flac16**: taped by See Notes; transferred by SIRMick; source: See Notes [2]. Also: Remaster of shnid 12222: DC offset removed, audience-source left channel boosted 2.4 dB, dropouts and clicks repaired, transitions cleaned [2]
- **gd1973-08-01.aud.weiner.8724.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Uher mic > Uher 4000 Report L 5" reels > MacIntosh pre-amp > TEAC 1230 7" reel.; transferred by A > D transfer by Noah Weiner; source: AudMR > R > DAT > WAV > SHN [10]. Also: First 1:06 of Dark Star came from an alternate audience source on Jeff Siniawsky's 7-inch reel, cross-faded into the main source [10]
- **gd1973-08-01.sbd.kaplan.11813.shnf**: taped by ** - CD Mastering by David Gans; transferred by Extraction and.shn encoding by Seth Kaplan via EAC and MKW.; source: SBD>MSR>R2>D>CD and SBD>7.5ips Master Reel>Cassette>20 bit A/D>CDR [11]. Also: Three-disc soundboard compilation, mastered by David Gans, adds soundboard segments beyond the earlier circulating one-disc Dark Star through Dew jam [11]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Bob Marks Grateful Dead: [1973-08-01 Roosevelt Stadium, Jersey City, NJ, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1973-08-01-roosevelt-stadium-jersey-city-nj-usa/) [27]
